author: DOC-029 source-review author agent (admin-org)
limitations: Source inspection only. No browser walkthrough was run. The independent walkthrough agent must replay V-C36, V-C37 and V-C55 against the recorded content hashes before any article can return to verified.

The authentication-and-email and organisation-and-users changes alter actions, prerequisites and results. They are not copy-only corrections, so earlier DOC-020 walkthrough evidence cannot be retained for them.
The dev text of authentication-and-email was reviewed. Another session edits the same article in the main checkout, and that text was not reviewed here.

corrections.before: The recipient sets a password for built-in sign-in; with OIDC configured the colleague can sign in through the identity provider.
corrections.after: The recipient sets a password. When Legal User Authentication has Single sign-on (SSO) turned on, the colleague can sign in through the identity provider instead.
corrections.reason: Commit fc241fcb replaced the exclusive built-in/OIDC mode with independent group policies (TECH-008 amendment). SSO sign-in for staff now depends on the legal policy's sso switch.

corrections.before: The row becomes Active after activation or sign-in.
corrections.after: The row becomes Active after the colleague sets a password or signs in through single sign-on. An email magic link sign-in alone leaves the row Invited with Resend invite and Revoke invite; do not revoke the invite of a colleague who already works in OpenLaw.
corrections.reason: users/routes.ts statusOf derives Invited from a staff role with no accounts row. Magic-link verification creates a session but no accounts row, and the legal policy can now allow staff magic links. This is reported as a product bug.

corrections.location: Change a role or revoke sessions, promotion paragraph
corrections.before: Where single sign-on is configured, an invited account can activate through the identity provider.
corrections.after: Where Legal User Authentication has Single sign-on (SSO) turned on, an invited account can activate through the identity provider.

corrections.location: Change a role or revoke sessions, session paragraph
corrections.before: Use the row's Revoke all sessions action. The account can sign in again using its configured method.
corrections.after: Use the row's Sign out user action. The account can sign in again with a sign-in method that its group allows. Your own row has no Sign out user or Archive action.
corrections.reason: Commit cab4dd77 gave the row action the visible label 'Sign out user' (settings.users.action.signOut). Its accessible name stays 'Revoke all sessions of {email}'. The row actions are hidden on the signed-in Administrator's own row.

confirmed: General: Organization name commits on Enter or blur, Escape restores the saved value, an empty name reverts.
General: Upload beside Logo accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG up to 256 KB; other files show the error state.
General: Default locale offers only English (United States); Default timezone commits through the timezone picker.
General and Users loaders redirect non-Administrators to /settings/profile; the API routes require the administrator role.
Invite user dialog: Display name, Email, Role radios Legal team member and Administrator only, Send invite. Contributor was removed by DD-023 and is no longer an invitable role.
Invite refusals: 'This user has already activated their account.' and 'This user already exists with a different role.'; a same-role pending address resends without a duplicate row.
Invited rows carry Resend invite and Revoke invite; revoke deletes the pending user row.
The role dropdown appears on Active rows only and offers Administrator, Legal team member and Business user; the change applies on the target's next request.
Last-Administrator guards: 'You cannot demote the last Administrator.', 'You cannot archive the last Administrator.', 'You cannot archive yourself.'
Archive deletes the user's sessions and the session-create hook refuses archived users; Show archived appears once an archived row exists; Restore does not bring revoked sessions back.
Archiving does not reassign records, Tasks, Obligations or Approvals.
No change to approver-groups or contract-approvals API code between 6a8873db and 3fa407e3.
Path: user menu Settings, Contracts section, Approver groups tab (/settings/contracts/approver-groups).
Add group opens 'Add approver group' with Name, Description and Members; submit label Add group; edit submit label Save; row Edit control is named 'Edit {name}'.
Member candidates are Administrators and Legal team members; ineligible saved members show 'Can no longer approve'. After DD-023 a lower role means Business user.
Groups list in name order; no reordering.
Contract record Approvals tab holds the Approvals & signing card; Apply group appears only when a live group exists and the Contract is not archived.
Apply approver group dialog: Approver group picker, 'Asks {names}.', skip count text, snapshot warning, Apply group submit.

Apply skips archived members and members with a pending request; refuses the whole action by name for a member who is not an Administrator or Legal Team Member, or who cannot see a confidential Contract; refuses an empty group or one whose members all have pending requests.
Editing saves name/description first, then members in a second request ('The member list could not be saved.').
Archive dialog confirms with Archive group and needs no replacement; Show archived and Restore return the group.

sources: docs/decision-records/DECISIONS-TECH-STACK.md (TECH-008 group authentication amendment; TECH-011 email precedence)

corrections.before: Choose staff sign-in and Business Portal access.
corrections.after: Choose how Administrators, Legal Team Members, and Business Users sign in.
corrections.reason: The pane now holds two group policy cards.

corrections.location: Section 'Choose built-in sign-in' (renamed 'Choose sign-in methods for each group'; no inbound links used the old anchor)
corrections.before: Select Built-in for staff password sign-in. Magic links are the Portal floor in built-in mode and the switch cannot turn them off.
corrections.after: Legal User Authentication and Business Portal Authentication each have Email and password, Email magic link, Single sign-on (SSO) and Require two-factor authentication switches that apply immediately. At least one method is required. SSO needs a registered provider. Administrators keep emergency password sign-in. Required two-factor applies to every method. Staff magic links ignore the allowed-domain list.
corrections.reason: Commit fc241fcb removed the Built-in / Identity provider (OIDC) mode radios and the Portal access magic-link toggle. PATCH /auth/policy/{group} refuses a policy with no method ('Enable at least one sign-in method.') and SSO without a provider.

corrections.before: Select Identity provider (OIDC), enter the fields, Register provider; registration completes the pending switch to OIDC.
corrections.after: Enter the fields in the Identity provider card and Register provider; registration turns on nothing. Then turn on Single sign-on (SSO) under Legal User Authentication, and under Business Portal Authentication if Business Users use it.
corrections.reason: saveProvider no longer calls a mode switch; the SSO switch is a per-group policy value.

corrections.before: Use Administrator password sign-in to recover and select Built-in.
corrections.after: Use Administrator password sign-in, turn on Email and password under Legal User Authentication, and turn off Single sign-on (SSO) if needed.
corrections.reason: Built-in mode no longer exists in the pane.

corrections.before: The list is checked every time a magic link is issued and blocks everyone on a removed domain.
corrections.after: The list is checked for magic links to Business Users and to addresses with no account. It does not limit existing Administrator or Legal Team Member accounts.
corrections.reason: POST /auth/magic-link and magicLinkDenied skip the domain check for existing non-Business-User accounts.

corrections.before: Existing Business Users keep sessions, earlier links and SSO. New entrants are refused a link or at first redemption/SSO callback. Use Revoke all sessions.
corrections.after: Adds password sign-in for Business Users with a password (when the group allows it), refusal of password setup links and password setup completion for unapproved new addresses, and the Sign out user label.
corrections.reason: Business password setup (authentication-policy-routes.ts) now exists and re-checks the domain on completion; the Users row action label changed.

corrections.before: In OIDC mode, Magic-link sign-in can be turned off.
corrections.after: Under Business Portal Authentication, turn off Email magic link to require another method. Links sent earlier stop working.
corrections.reason: The group policy replaces the OIDC-only toggle; /magic-link/verify checks the account's group magicLink option at redemption.

corrections.location: Set up email before finishing the wizard, closing paragraph
corrections.before: Complete the checks before finishing or selecting Set up later on the Welcome or final invitation step.
corrections.after: The wizard cannot finish until email is configured. Outbound email has no Set up later and Continue stays unavailable. Skip optional steps opens Outbound email while email is unconfigured. A configured relay does not prove delivery.
corrections.reason: welcome.tsx hides Set up later on the email step, disables Continue until email is configured, and finish() routes to the email step; POST /onboarding/complete refuses with 'Configure outbound email before finishing instance setup.'

confirmed: Settings rail: Organization, Security, Authentication at /settings/authentication; loader redirects non-Administrators.

Provider form labels Provider ID, Issuer URL, Email domain, Client ID, Client secret; Register provider then Save provider; blank Client secret keeps the stored secret; Provider ID is not editable after registration.
Callback text 'Paste this callback URL into your IdP console'; redirect URI is the shared /api/auth/sso/callback.
The identity provider only authenticates; staff roles come from OpenLaw; SSO JIT creation admits only allowed-domain Business Users when Business Portal Authentication allows SSO.
Allowed email domains with Add and per-entry Remove {domain}; empty-list text 'No domains allowed yet. Magic-link sign-in is unavailable.'
Outbound email step labels: SMTP relay URL, From address, Save relay, Send test email (to the signed-in Administrator), Replace relay, Keep current relay, Clear relay.
Environment precedence: SMTP_URL makes the step read-only; SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM shows the incomplete warning; PUT /email-settings refuses while the environment sets SMTP.
The welcome loader redirects once onboarding is complete; onboarding step email has no settingsPath, so no email Settings page exists.
Authentication Settings do not hold e-signature or AI connector settings.
